newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: GOVERNMENT AGREES TO 50 MLN MARKKA CREDIT.
newsitem.headline: GOVERNMENT AGREES TO 50 MLN MARKKA CREDIT.

text.p: The Lithuanian government said on Tuesday it would take up Finland's 1992 offer of a 50 million Finnish markka credit and use the money to buy medical equipment.

"Finland's 1992, 50 million markka credit was not used because the conditions for providing the credit allowed only the purchase of Finnish railway cars and other goods that were too expensive," the government's press office said in a statement.
The Lithuanian and Finnish prime ministers agreed to the new purpose of the credit during their meeting in Vilnius on Monday, the statement said.
The statement did not give the terms of the credit.
